quote: People can stand what is true,for they are already enduring it.
content: Fable's Huntington's example was tested, and it came out the litany's way. In the Canadian predictive-testing programme, people who learned their status, whether at increased risk or decreased risk, showed better psychological well-being a year later than those who remained uncertain (Wiggins et al. 1992). The carrier who has not been tested is already enduring the disease that is coming, and the uncertainty is an extra burden that knowing removes. Owning up to it did not make it worse, and for the increased-risk group it made things better. Information avoidance exists, as Golman et al. document, but it is a choice people make, not evidence about what people can stand. The litany speaks to the second question.
